tool_input.command: ls -la test/ && ls -la && npm test 2>&1 | head -50
tool_input.description: List test directory and run npm test

result:
The full test suite is off-limits here per project convention (targeted tests only), and the actual test files (`test/parse.test.js`, `test/fmt.test.js`) are empty stubs with no assertions, plus `package.json`'s `test` script points at a `test/run.js` that doesn't exist — so there's no runnable test harness to invoke.

I ran a targeted manual check directly against `src/parse.js` instead:

- `exports.parse = s => new Date(s)` — unchanged, just wraps `Date`.
- Valid ISO dates (`"2024-01-15"`, `"2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"`) parse correctly.
- Invalid input (`"not a date"`, `""`) correctly yields `Invalid Date`.

The parser behaves as expected. Note: there's no actual test coverage for `parse.js` in this repo (the test files are empty placeholders) — if you want real regression protection, I can add assertions to `test/parse.test.js`, but I didn't do that since you only asked me to check it still works.
